ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A hollow sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is placed under a plank of mass $3 M$ and length $2 R$. The plank is hinged to the floor, and it initially makes an angle $\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$ rad to the horizontal. Under the weight of the plank, the sphere starts rolling without slipping across the floor. What is the sphere's initial translational acceleration? Assume the plank is frictionless.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the ground is horizontal, there is a hinge at the left end, a slender wooden board is inclined upward to the right from the hinge, and its angle with the horizontal ground is θ; a hollow sphere with radius R and mass M is below the wooden board, the sphere contacts both the ground and the wooden board, and the wooden board is tangent to the sphere. Reasoning: Take the board angle θ as the only generalized coordinate according to the specified method. From the tangent-line geometry in the figure, the wooden board can be regarded as a straight line passing through the hinge, the height of the sphere center is always R, and the horizontal coordinate of the sphere center is x(θ)=R cot(θ/2). Therefore dx/dθ=-(R/2)csc^2(θ/2), and when θ=π/3, dx/dθ=-2R. The wooden board has mass 3M and length 2R, and its moment of inertia about the hinge is I=(1/3)(3M)(2R)^2=4MR^2. When the hollow sphere rolls, I_sphere=(2/3)MR^2, so the kinetic energy of the sphere is (1/2)M xdot^2+(1/2)(2/3 MR^2)(xdot/R)^2=5/6 M xdot^2. Since xdot=(dx/dθ)θdot, the equivalent inertia of the system with respect to θ is 4MR^2+(5/3)M(dx/dθ)^2. The center of mass of the wooden board is R from the hinge, and the potential energy V=3MgR sinθ; the height of the sphere center is unchanged, and the gravitational potential energy of the sphere is unchanged. At the instant of release θdot=0, the Lagrange equation gives [4MR^2+(5/3)M(dx/dθ)^2]θddot+3MgR cosθ=0. Substitute θ=π/3: the equivalent inertia is 4MR^2+(5/3)M(4R^2)=32MR^2/3, and 3MgR cos(π/3)=3MgR/2, so θddot=-(3MgR/2)/(32MR^2/3)=-9g/(64R). The initial translational acceleration of the sphere is a=xddot=(dx/dθ)θddot=(-2R)(-9g/(64R))=9g/32≈0.281g. Taking g=9.8 m/s^2, a≈2.76 m/s^2, directed to the right.

raw_record.question_text: A hollow sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is placed under a plank of mass $3M$ and length $2R$. The plank is hinged to the floor, and it initially makes an angle $\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}$ rad to the horizontal. method.method_draft: Use a single generalized coordinate, the plank angle θ. From the image, model the plank as a line through the hinge tangent to the sphere whose center is at height R above the floor. The tangency geometry gives the sphere center’s horizontal coordinate x(θ)=R cot(θ/2), so initially at θ=π/3, dx/dθ=−2R. Write kinetic energy as plank rotation plus rolling sphere: I_plank about hinge = (1/3)(3M)(2R)^2=4MR^2, and for a hollow rolling sphere T_sphere = 1/2 M xdot^2 + 1/2(2/3 MR^2)(xdot/R)^2 = 5/6 M xdot^2. Thus the effective inertia in θ is 4MR^2+(5/3)M(dx/dθ)^2. The only changing potential energy is the plank’s, V=3Mg(R sinθ), since its center of mass is R from the hinge. Apply Lagrange’s equation at release, where θdot=0, so [4MR^2+(5/3)M(dx/dθ)^2]θddot + 3MgR cosθ=0. Evaluate at θ=π/3 and convert sphere acceleration by a=xdotdot=(dx/dθ)θddot, obtaining a≈0.281g≈2.76 m/s^2.

method.method_draft: Use Newton–Euler equations with an explicit contact normal. From the image, locate the contact point along the plank using the tangent geometry: at θ=π/3 the contact distance from the hinge is q=R cot(θ/2)=√3R, and the line normal has horizontal component sinθ. Let N be the normal force between plank and sphere. For the sphere, the plank is frictionless, so the plank force has horizontal component N sinθ and passes through the sphere center; floor friction supplies the torque needed for rolling. Combine translation M a=N sinθ+f with rolling torque for a hollow shell, f=−(2/3)Ma, giving N sinθ=(5/3)Ma. For the plank, take torques about the hinge: I_plank α = qN − 3MgR cosθ, with I_plank=4MR^2. Finally impose the instantaneous kinematic constraint from tangency, a=(dx/dθ)α=−2Rα at θ=π/3. Solve these simultaneous equations to get a=0.28125g≈2.76 m/s^2.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The figure shows a horizontal floor, a hinge at the left end of a straight plank, and the plank inclined upward to the right at angle θ. A hollow sphere of mass M and radius R rests on the floor under the plank, touching the plank tangentially. The contact between sphere and plank is on the upper-left side of the sphere, and the plank is frictionless, so the contact force is normal to the plank.

Reasoning: Use the tangent geometry shown in the image. For a circle of radius R tangent to the floor and to a line through the hinge at angle θ, the distance along the plank to the contact point is q = R cot(θ/2). At θ = π/3, q = R cot(π/6) = √3 R. The normal to the plank has horizontal component sinθ, so the horizontal component of the plank force on the sphere is N sinθ.

For the hollow sphere, I = (2/3)MR². The plank is frictionless, so its force N passes through the center of the sphere and gives no torque about the sphere center. Floor friction f gives the rolling torque. Taking rightward translational acceleration as a, the horizontal force equation is M a = N sinθ + f. Rolling without slipping gives f = -(I/R²) M? More directly, fR = Iα_rot and α_rot = -a/R, so f = -(2/3)Ma. Therefore M a = N sinθ - (2/3)Ma, hence N sinθ = (5/3)Ma.

For the plank, take torque about the hinge. Its moment of inertia is I_plank = (1/3)(3M)(2R)² = 4MR². The normal force from the sphere gives torque qN, while the plank weight 3Mg acts at its midpoint, distance R from the hinge, giving clockwise torque 3MgR cosθ. Thus 4MR² α = qN - 3MgR cosθ.

At θ = π/3, sinθ = √3/2 and cosθ = 1/2. From N sinθ = (5/3)Ma, N = (10/(3√3))Ma. Substitute into the plank equation: 4MR² α = (√3R)(10/(3√3)Ma) - 3MgR(1/2) = (10/3)MaR - (3/2)MgR.

The instantaneous tangency constraint gives the sphere center position x = R cot(θ/2), so at θ = π/3, dx/dθ = -2R. Since the system starts from rest, a = (dx/dθ)α = -2Rα. Substitute α = -a/(2R): 4MR²(-a/(2R)) = (10/3)MaR - (3/2)MgR. So -2a = (10/3)a - (3/2)g. Therefore -(16/3)a = -(3/2)g, giving a = (9/32)g = 0.28125g. With g = 9.8 m/s², a ≈ 2.76 m/s².

At θ = π/3, sinθ = √3/2 and cosθ = 1/2. From N sinθ = (5/3)Ma, N = (10/(3√3))Ma. Substitute into the plank equation: 4MR² α = (√3R)(10/(3√3)Ma) - 3MgR(1/2) = (10/3)MaR - (3/2)MgR.

The instantaneous tangency constraint gives the sphere center position x = R cot(θ/2), so at θ = π/3, dx/dθ = -2R. Since the system starts from rest, a = (dx/dθ)α = -2Rα. Substitute α = -a/(2R): 4MR²(-a/(2R)) = (10/3)MaR - (3/2)MgR. So -2a = (10/3)a - (3/2)g. Therefore -(16/3)a = -(3/2)g, giving a = (9/32)g = 0.28125g. With g = 9.8 m/s², a ≈ 2.76 m/s².

raw_record.original_question: A hollow sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is placed under a plank of mass $3M$ and length $2R$. The plank is hinged to the floor, and it initially makes an angle $\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}$ rad to the horizontal. Under the weight of the plank, the sphere starts rolling without slipping across the floor. What is the sphere's initial translational acceleration? Assume the plank is frictionless.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the ground is horizontal, there is a hinge at the left end, a slender wooden board is inclined upward to the right from the hinge, and its angle with the horizontal ground is θ; a hollow sphere with radius R and mass M is below the wooden board, the sphere contacts both the ground and the wooden board, and the wooden board is tangent to the sphere. Reasoning: Take the board angle θ as the only generalized coordinate according to the specified method. From the tangent-line geometry in the figure, the wooden board can be regarded as a straight line passing through the hinge, the height of the sphere center is always R, and the horizontal coordinate of the sphere center is x(θ)=R cot(θ/2). Therefore dx/dθ=-(R/2)csc^2(θ/2), and when θ=π/3, dx/dθ=-2R. The wooden board has mass 3M and length 2R, and its moment of inertia about the hinge is I=(1/3)(3M)(2R)^2=4MR^2. When the hollow sphere rolls, I_sphere=(2/3)MR^2, so the kinetic energy of the sphere is (1/2)M xdot^2+(1/2)(2/3 MR^2)(xdot/R)^2=5/6 M xdot^2. Since xdot=(dx/dθ)θdot, the equivalent inertia of the system with respect to θ is 4MR^2+(5/3)M(dx/dθ)^2. The center of mass of the wooden board is R from the hinge, and the potential energy V=3MgR sinθ; the height of the sphere center is unchanged, and the gravitational potential energy of the sphere is unchanged. At the instant of release θdot=0, the Lagrange equation gives [4MR^2+(5/3)M(dx/dθ)^2]θddot+3MgR cosθ=0. Substitute θ=π/3: the equivalent inertia is 4MR^2+(5/3)M(4R^2)=32MR^2/3, and 3MgR cos(π/3)=3MgR/2, so θddot=-(3MgR/2)/(32MR^2/3)=-9g/(64R). The initial translational acceleration of the sphere is a=xddot=(dx/dθ)θddot=(-2R)(-9g/(64R))=9g/32≈0.281g. Taking g=9.8 m/s^2, a≈2.76 m/s^2, directed to the right.
